chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Muhrim (one in Ihram) who takes a bath, so he said, 'Yes, he pours water over his head and does not rub it.'

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (sacred consecration for pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rubbing the head while bathing in Ihram?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith clarifies the prohibition of *dalak* (rubbing/scrubbing) specifically for the head during Ihram, distinguishing it from the permissible act of pouring water (*ifu'*). This ruling is central to the Shia jurisprudence of Hajj, emphasizing that while washing is allowed, the mechanical action of rubbing the head is restricted to preserve the sanctity of the state of consecration.
